subject: Workplace Skills
title: Speaking Up in Meetings
description: A 60-second lesson on Speaking Up in Meetings.

hook.text: Research shows the person who speaks first in a meeting anchors the entire discussion.

buildup.text: Many people stay silent because they fear saying something obvious or wrong in front of peers.

discovery.text: Prepared talking points eliminate anxiety. Write two sentences before the meeting and read them if needed.

twist.text: Asking a clarifying question counts as speaking up. You don't need a brilliant insight, just engagement.

climax.text: Speak in the first five minutes. The longer you wait, the harder it feels and the less impact you make.

punchline.text: Speak early. A question counts. Silence is invisible.

quiz.question: Why is speaking early in a meeting important?
options: It proves you are the most knowledgeable person in the room
The first speaker anchors the discussion and waiting makes it harder
Meeting rules require everyone to speak in order
